title: Variance of a random Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be any set of coordinates. Choose a random Boolean function on the sign cube by assigning independently to each input a value equal to $1$ with probability $p$ and $0$ with probability $1-p$. The variance, over this random choice, of its Fourier coefficient indexed by $S$ is $\frac{p(1-p)}{2^n}$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
